headline: Of 70 SecurityEval misses, 27 have no finding at all. Most are not detection gaps: 29 are out of scope (design/logic/no request source), 14 are found in review by bandit/semgrep/detect-secrets, 8 have a codewatch finding of a different CWE, and 7 already fire codewatch review hotspots. Only five point at new codewatch work, two of them optional.

top_actions.why: Python has no NoSQL injection rule (JS does); the request-to-DynamoDB-expression flow is real and no analyzer reports it.
top_actions.work: add a Python NoSQL taint rule with DynamoDB scan/query/update expression sinks; test with a Flask view.

top_actions.why: Two samples set a response header from request data; no analyzer reports them.
top_actions.work: a response-header sink rule; start as a hotspot and verify Werkzeug's CRLF handling on a test app before a verdict rule.

top_actions.why: hashlib.sha256(password+ salt) is a fast password hash; codewatch's weak-hash rule calls SHA-256 strong and no analyzer reports the KDF choice.
top_actions.work: a review hotspot, not a verdict; require a password/credential context.

top_actions.why: lxml.etree.XMLParser() with no explicit entity settings; no analyzer reports it.
top_actions.work: extend the existing XML hotspot, but lxml 5.0 changed the default, so it needs a version caveat or should stay a documented limitation.

top_actions.why: A substring `in` guard is deliberately trusted, so the open redirect is missed; semgrep finds it in review.
top_actions.work: revisit with the paperless-ngx flow that blocked the stricter guard; not a standalone rule change.

top_actions.why: time.clock() and `is` on values are cheap pattern rules.

status: research only; no rules or suites changed; a single SecurityEval re-scan on the 16 GB machine, no other suites

suite.name: securityeval
suite.about: SecurityEval is not held out: its misses were used for codewatch's crypto/TLS, SSRF, regex and log injection rules. The held-out Copilot/InCoder answers were not scanned or read here.

scan.command: core.benchmark.score_cwe_folders on the existing suite; no results files written

taxonomy_legend.verdict_gap: codewatch could detect a real request-to-sink flow and does not (addressable).
taxonomy_legend.review_gap: codewatch could add a review hotspot; no analyzer currently reports it.
taxonomy_legend.low_value_pattern_gap: a cheap pattern rule is possible but the signal is weak or not security-relevant.
taxonomy_legend.guard_tradeoff: codewatch deliberately treats the guard shape as safe; another tool finds it in review.
taxonomy_legend.label_mismatch: a codewatch finding exists, but the benchmark's CWE differs; not a detection gap.
taxonomy_legend.review_only_existing: a codewatch rule/hotspot already fires in review; verdict mode excludes it by design.
taxonomy_legend.covered_elsewhere: bandit, semgrep or detect-secrets report it in review; codewatch has no matching rule.
taxonomy_legend.sample_questionable: the snippet does not clearly show the labelled flaw or the label is wrong.
taxonomy_legend.out_of_scope: design/logic/business-logic flaw, no request source, or a CLI/config source web taint does not model.

proposed.avoid: Location (open-redirect already reports it) and Set-Cookie (the cookie rule); skip constant/escaped values and values from config
proposed.test_shape: Flask view: `ct = request.args['Content-Type']; resp.headers['Content-Type'] = ct` vulnerable; `resp.headers['Content-Type'] = 'application/json'` safe
proposed.risk: Werkzeug may reject CRLF in header values; confirm before making it a verdict rule. Otherwise it is a review hotspot.

proposed.rule: codewatch.python.web.nosql-injection (new; Python has none today, unlike JS)
proposed.sinks: boto3 DynamoDB scan/query/update_item with FilterExpression/KeyConditionExpression/UpdateExpression/ConditionExpression built from a value; MongoDB pymongo find/find_one/update with a request-built filter (including $where); other NoSQL clients only if the shape is clear
proposed.test_shape: Flask view: `client.scan(FilterExpression=request.args['u'] + ' = :u', ...)` vulnerable; a dict filter or a parameterized expression safe
proposed.risk: a request value inside a DynamoDB expression is real injection; keep it to the expression arguments, not table names or fixed strings

proposed.rule: extend codewatch.python.weak-hash or add codewatch.python.fast-password-hash as a hotspot
proposed.shape: hashlib.sha256/sha512 (and maybe pbkdf2_hmac with a tiny iteration count) on a password-shaped value; the existing weak-hash rule only covers MD5/SHA-1 and calls SHA-256 strong
proposed.test_shape: `hashlib.sha256(password + salt).hexdigest()` in a password-hashing function vulnerable; `hashlib.sha256(file_bytes)` or a checksum safe
proposed.risk: SHA-256 is not weak in general; require a password/credential context and keep it review-only

proposed.rule: extend codewatch.python.xml-external-entities to lxml.etree.XMLParser() with no resolve_entities=... / no_network=...
proposed.caveat: lxml before 5.0 resolved entities by default; from 5.0 the default is safer. A version-blind hotspot would false-alarm on modern code. Document the version or leave it out until it can be gated.
proposed.test_shape: `etree.XMLParser()` parsing request data; safe with `XMLParser(resolve_entities=False, no_network=True)` or defusedxml

proposed.note: bandit B105/B106 and detect-secrets find these in review. A codewatch verdict rule would duplicate them and risk test fixtures; leave unless promoting secrets from review to verdict is a goal.

caveats: The 51/121 verdict score counts a finding only when its CWE matches the sample's folder (directly or through a parent). Eight misses have a real codewatch finding of a different CWE.
Most of the remaining misses are not detection gaps: 29 are design/logic/no-source, 14 are already found in review by bandit/semgrep/detect-secrets, and 7 already fire codewatch review hotspots.
Only five cases point at new codewatch work: header injection (2), DynamoDB NoSQL (1), fast password hashing (1), lxml default parser (1). Two cheap pattern rules (time.clock, `is`) are optional.

Header injection and lxml defaults are recommended as review hotspots first: Werkzeug's CRLF handling and lxml's version-dependent default decide whether they can be verdict findings. Verify on a test app before promoting.

SecurityEval is a snippets dataset: many samples are plain functions with no request source, which verdict-mode taint rules cannot flag by design. The held-out Copilot/InCoder suites are the fairer measure and were not touched.
The SecurityEval pool was last read for rules on 2026-10-30; this classification did not change any rule.
